children: Consumer confidence in New Zealand improved in the third quarter but remains below its 10-year average as households continue to be buffeted by powerful financial headwinds, a survey showed on Wednesday.
The Westpac McDermott Miller consumer confidence index rose to 89.5 from 80.4 in the previous quarter.
A reading above 100 indicates more optimists than pessimists.
